sector: Real Estate / Diversified REIT & Fund Manager
overview: Stride Property Group is an NZX-listed stapled entity combining Stride Property Limited (SPL), a diversified New Zealand commercial property owner across office, town centre and industrial assets, with Stride Investment Management Limited (SIML), an external funds manager. SPL directly owns a ~$1.1bn office and town-centre portfolio and holds cornerstone stakes in the vehicles SIML manages, giving a combined look-through investment portfolio of ~$1.4bn and combined managed portfolio value across all Stride Products of ~$2.4bn. NZX designates the stapled security 'Non-Standard' (NS); fiscal year ends 31 March.

business_model.summary: Two-legged model: SPL earns net rental income from directly owned office and town centre property plus equity-accounted income/dividends from its stakes in Investore (18.8%), the Industre industrial joint venture (49.0%) and Diversified NZ Property Fund (2.2%); SIML earns external recurring asset management fees plus activity-based fees (leasing, development, transactions) from managing those same vehicles for third-party capital. The fee stream is capital-light and higher-margin than the property-owning leg and should be valued on a funds-management multiple, not a REIT cap-rate/NTA multiple, because it scales with AUM and activity rather than requiring balance-sheet capital.

revenue_streams.name: SPL net rental income (directly owned property)
revenue_streams.note: FY26 net rental income $58.9m, down from $69.1m in FY25 due to the Silverdale Centre divestment (-$2.7m) and Industre restructure (-$3.9m)

revenue_streams.name: SIML recurring management fees
revenue_streams.note: FY26 recurring fees $17.5m vs $16.5m FY25; grows with AUM of open-ended Products

revenue_streams.name: SIML activity-based fees
revenue_streams.note: FY26 $5.4m vs $3.9m FY25; tied to leasing, development and transaction activity in the managed Products

revenue_streams.name: SPL equity-accounted income from Investore/Industre/Diversified
revenue_streams.note: Distributable profit driven higher in FY26 by increased Industre dividends; look-through revenue split shown as 36% office/retail rent, with management fees ~21% of look-through revenue

business_model.customer_type: Institutional/wholesale unit- and shareholders in the managed Products (Investore is NZX-listed and open to retail; Diversified is a closed-end trust majority-owned by two Australian superannuation funds; Industre is a JV with JPMAM) plus direct commercial tenants (offices, town centre retail, industrial) across office, retail and industrial B2B leasing
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand; concentrated in Auckland and Wellington office/town centre, with Investore's convenience retail and Industre's industrial assets also NZ-wide (Industre concentrated in the Auckland region)

main_competitors: independent NZ fund managers competing for institutional mandates
competitive_position.market_position: Mid-sized diversified NZ-listed property owner and one of a small number of internally-aligned external property fund managers in the NZX-listed REIT sector; SIML manages ~$2.4bn of committed Product AUM (external AUM ~$2.0-2.4bn) spanning office, convenience retail, industrial and diversified shopping centres

moat_factors.description: SPL holds meaningful equity stakes in every vehicle SIML manages (18.8% Investore, 49.0% Industre, 2.2% Diversified), aligning manager and capital-partner interests and giving Stride 'significant influence' board representation that supports mandate retention, but also creates related-party governance scrutiny

Long-dated management agreements (Investore's initial term was 10 years from the 2016 stapling) and deep operational integration (leasing, development, asset management delivered in-house) raise the cost of internalising or re-tendering management, but mandates are not permanently locked in and largest external vehicle relationships face periodic review points

moat_factors.factor: Scale and track record in NZ listed property funds management
moat_factors.description: One of a small number of established, multi-decade NZ property managers with in-house origination, leasing, asset management and development capability across four Products
Long operating history (SPL predecessors date back decades) and high GRESB score (79/100, up 10 points in FY26) support institutional credibility
Fee income requires little incremental balance-sheet capital versus a traditional REIT, so management fee growth can outpace property capex

weaknesses: Small scale relative to larger NZX REITs (Goodman Property Trust, Precinct) limits pricing power and bidding capacity for large mandates or assets

Complex, opaque stapled structure with cross-holdings and related-party transactions (e.g., SPL selling Silverdale Centre to Investore, which SIML manages) invites governance and conflict-of-interest scrutiny
Office portfolio occupancy declined to 85.7% (from 87.7%) with cap rates softening to 6.2% (from 5.9%), reflecting structural weak demand for secondary/lower-tier office space
Diversified fund's 10-year anniversary review in 2026 could see unitholders vote to wind it up, directly removing a management fee stream

Reliance on continued willingness of external capital partners (JPMAM in Industre, Australian super funds in Diversified, NZX shareholders in Investore) to retain SIML as manager rather than internalise

growth_drivers: Growth in committed/external AUM: open-ended Products (Investore, Industre, Diversified) grew portfolios by more than $200m in FY26, driving recurring fee growth

North Wharf, Wynyard Quarter, Auckland: conditional 125-year prepaid ground lease (~$17.5m) for a 10,500-12,500 sqm premium mixed-use retail/office redevelopment, partnered with Ngati Whatua Orakei; resource consent expected 2027

Industre industrial development pipeline: ~$70m (excluding land) project at 2-14 Patiki Road, Auckland targeted for FY27/28 subject to final construction pricing, following completion of 16A Wickham Street (Hamilton) and 14-20 Favona Road (Auckland) developments valued at $93.7m
Investore's expanded investment mandate from large-format retail into convenience-based retail, widening its acquisition pipeline (Silverdale Centre $114m from SPL, Bunnings New Lynn $43m)

Asset recycling: SPL selling non-core/lower-growth assets (Silverdale Centre, Woolworths Browns Bay/New Brighton, agreed sale of Woolworths Greenlane) to fund higher-return opportunities and reduce leverage, while retaining management income where sold to a Stride Product

Office portfolio repositioning at 34 Shortland Street and 215 Lambton Quay (building upgrades, higher WALT of 6.7 years vs 4.6 years in 2020, 93% premium-grade by value) to support leasing and rental growth
Activity-based fees scale with transaction, leasing and development activity across the Products, providing operating leverage on top of recurring base fees
Undrawn $166m bank facility with no debt maturities until FY30 gives balance-sheet capacity to fund growth without near-term refinancing risk

business.description: Occupancy fell to 85.7% (from 87.7%) and office cap rates softened to 6.2% (from 5.9%) in FY26; hybrid working and flight-to-quality continue to pressure secondary office assets

business.risk: Loss of managed mandates / fund wind-ups
business.description: Diversified NZ Property Fund reaches its 10-year review in 2026; if unitholders vote to wind it up, SIML's management agreement terminates on sale of all properties, cutting Stride's normalised distributable profit by an estimated 5-6%
SPL both owns stakes in and sells assets to the vehicles SIML manages (e.g., Silverdale Centre sold by SPL to Investore), requiring careful governance to avoid perceived self-dealing

business.risk: Small scale versus larger NZX REIT peers
business.description: Limits ability to compete for very large mandates, assets or capital raisings against Goodman Property Trust, Precinct Properties and Kiwi Property

financial.description: SPL bank LVR was 34% at 31 March 2026 (down from 39%), with balance-sheet gearing (including Product interests) at 24% and look-through gearing at 35%; further cap-rate declines would erode headroom

financial.risk: Interest rate reset risk on unfixed debt
financial.description: 95% of SPL's drawn debt was fixed at 31 March 2026 (up from 72%) at a 5.04% weighted average cost of borrowings; the remaining floating portion and future refinancing at maturity (though none until FY30) remain exposed to rate cycles

financial.risk: NTA erosion and impairments on associate stakes
financial.description: NTA per share fell to $1.69 (from $1.72); SPL recognised a further $2.1m impairment on its Investore investment in FY26 (following an $8.8m impairment in FY25) as Investore's share price trades below carrying value

regulatory.description: NZX has designated SPL, SIML and the stapled Stride security 'Non-Standard' given the stapled structure, requiring specific waivers and disclosure; this can weigh on institutional investor appetite and index inclusion

regulatory.risk: Resource consent risk on North Wharf
regulatory.description: The Auckland Council ground lease is conditional on resource consent, expected in 2027; delay, refusal or cost escalation would defer or impair the development opportunity
Management notes the Investment Boost tax deduction as an important input to development feasibility; policy changes could alter returns on the development pipeline

macro.risk: NZ interest rate and economic cycle
macro.description: Management does not expect a material change in economic recovery until H2 2027 at the earliest; a slower-for-longer recovery weighs on leasing demand, rental growth and cap rates
FY26 outlook flagged recent offshore developments reintroducing inflation pressure and market uncertainty, weighing on NZ business and consumer confidence
Further cap-rate expansion (yield decompression) across office, retail and industrial would compress NTA, gearing headroom and the value of SPL's associate stakes across the sector broadly

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ commercial property is emerging cautiously from a multi-year down-cycle; office remains structurally weak (soft occupancy, rising vacancy in Auckland/Wellington secondary stock), while convenience retail and industrial (Investore, Industre) are showing more resilient fundamentals and cap-rate stability. Management does not expect a material economic recovery until at least H2 2027.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High for the direct property leg (rental growth, occupancy and valuations move with the NZ economic and interest-rate cycle); more resilient for the funds-management fee leg, which has a recurring base but activity fees are cyclical
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — cap rates, valuations, NTA and debt servicing costs are all directly sensitive to NZ OCR and long-term interest rate moves; SPL has substantially increased fixed-rate debt cover (95% fixed) to mitigate near-term cash flow risk

recent_developments.event: FY26 annual results: profit after tax $31.3m (up $9.6m on FY25's $21.7m); distributable profit $49.1m (up 2% on FY25's $48.3m); combined FY26 cash dividend 8.0cps at a 91.1% payout ratio; NTA per share $1.69, down from $1.72 at 31 March 2025
Management fee income grew 12% to $22.9m (FY25: $20.4m), driven by growth in Industre and Investore; SPL bank LVR improved to 34% (from 39%) following the Silverdale Centre sale

Conditional agreement with Auckland Council for a 125-year prepaid ground lease (~$17.5m) at North Wharf, Wynyard Quarter, to redevelop into a premium mixed-use retail and office asset in partnership with Ngati Whatua Orakei; resource consent submitted post balance date, expected 2027

SPL sold Silverdale Centre, Auckland to Investore for $114m (6.8% initial yield) while retaining management; Investore also acquired Bunnings New Lynn for $43m and expanded its mandate from large-format to convenience-based retail

Industre completed developments at 16A Wickham Street, Hamilton and (post balance date) 14-20 Favona Road, Auckland, together valued at $93.7m; committed to a further ~$70m development at 2-14 Patiki Road, Auckland for FY27/28

Board transition: David Green (ex-ANZ Singapore CEO, Chair of BT Funds Management NZ) joined the SPL/SIML boards in June 2025; Chair Tim Storey announced intention to step down by the 2026 AGM, with Green expected to succeed him

SPL continued to sell non-core assets — agreed post balance date to sell Woolworths Greenlane, Auckland for $35.9m, following the $31.8m sale of two Woolworths-tenanted properties (5.2% above book value)

Diversified NZ Property Fund approaches its 10-year anniversary review in 2026; unitholders may vote to wind it up, which management estimates would reduce Stride's normalised distributable profit by ~5-6% over the longer term

items.notes: Consistent with FY26's 8.0cps; subject to market conditions, and to the policy of paying 80-100% of SPL's distributable profit and 25-75% of SIML's distributable profit

items.target: No material change expected until H2 2027 at the earliest
items.notes: Management sees limited further downside from current levels but a slow recovery path given a subdued macro environment and renewed offshore inflation/uncertainty

items.target: Approximately 5-6% reduction in Stride's normalised distributable profit if Diversified is wound up
items.period: medium to long term, contingent on 2026 unitholder vote
items.notes: Near-term project/termination fees are expected to partially offset the loss of recurring management fees

items.target: ~$70m (excluding land) for Industre's Patiki Road development
items.notes: Subject to final construction pricing; North Wharf capex/timeline still to be confirmed pending resource consent (expected 2027)

guidance.management_commentary: The Chair and CEO said Stride enters FY27 with capacity to optimise its direct portfolio and drive growth across the platform, with near-term focus on progressing a build-to-core strategy, recycling non-core assets, active asset and capital management, and disciplined cost management. They noted a strong balance sheet with $166m of undrawn debt and no facility maturities until FY30, and flagged government policy settings (including the Investment Boost tax deduction) as important inputs to development feasibility. They remain mindful of ongoing volatility in global markets but believe Stride is well placed to navigate the current environment as conditions normalise.

bull_case: Trades at a meaningful discount to NTA ($1.69/share at 31 March 2026 vs a recent share price around $1.15-1.17, i.e. roughly a 30%+ discount), offering potential re-rating upside if the discount narrows

Capital-light, high-margin funds management fee stream (SIML) is growing faster than the directly-owned property leg (fee income up 12% in FY26) and deserves a fund-manager multiple rather than a pure REIT multiple, which the market may be under-appreciating

Well-covered, high dividend yield (~7%+) with an 8.0cps FY27 guided distribution and a strong balance sheet (34% bank LVR, $166m undrawn facilities, no debt maturities until FY30) provides income support and flexibility

Identifiable development pipeline (North Wharf, Industre's Patiki Road project) and asset recycling into higher-quality, better-let assets should support NTA and earnings growth once the NZ economic cycle turns

Cornerstone co-investment stakes in Investore, Industre and Diversified give SPL a diversified, largely non-office income stream (industrial and convenience retail) that has outperformed the direct office portfolio
bear_case: Office portfolio continues to deteriorate structurally (occupancy down to 85.7%, cap rates rising to 6.2%), and this segment remains a meaningful share of SPL's directly owned assets

Diversified's 10-year review in 2026 creates a concrete, dated risk of losing a management mandate outright, cutting distributable profit by an estimated 5-6% over the longer term, illustrating the broader existential risk that any Stride Product could eventually internalise or switch managers

Complex stapled structure with cross-holdings and related-party transactions (SPL selling assets to Investore, which SIML manages) creates governance complexity and may deter some institutional investors, contributing to a persistent NTA discount
NZ commercial property recovery is not expected until at least H2 2027 per management's own commentary, meaning earnings and valuation headwinds could persist for another 12-18+ months

Repeated impairments on the Investore stake (cumulative $29.3m) show that SPL's associate investments are directly exposed to weakness in the listed NZ REIT sector, and North Wharf's redevelopment upside is contingent on an uncertain 2027 resource consent outcome
